newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia property market picks up - survey.
newsitem.headline: Australia property market picks up - survey.

text.p: Australia's property market has strengthened over the past year, but would continue to be held back by the country's high unemployment rate, a leading industry group said on Sunday.
"The property market at the beginning of 1997 is much stronger than this time last year," the Real Estate Institute of Australia said in its latest market survey.

"House prices and rents are higher in most state capitals and vacancy rates are generally falling as demand for rental properties starts to outstrip supply in some areas," the institute's February survey said.

The institute, which did not speculate on the cause of the strengthening, said the median trend for house prices in the six state capitals and Canberra increased 2.9 percent over the past year, fuelled by a 9.8 percent rise in Sydney and a 6.7 percent rise in Melbourne.
House rents in the six state capitals and Canberra increased an average 5.1 percent over the past year and unit, or appartment, rents rose an average 6.1 percent.
But low inflation and modest economic growth would prevent prices hitting the highs of the 1980s, the institute said.
And Australia's high unemployment rate -- stuck around 8.5 percent -- would hold the property market back.

"Until the rate of jobs growth substantially increases, the current climate of employment uncertainty will continue to retard growth in the property market," institute president Don Brindley said in a statement.
